classification.difficultyReason: Explain why negative numbers have no real square roots using the sign of a square.

content.prompt: Type $\sqrt{-1}$ into the calculator. Try this with square roots of other negative numbers. Explain.

answer.short: In real-number mode, the calculator gives an error. A negative number has no real square root because the square of a real number is always non-negative.
answer.worked: In real-number mode, the calculator gives an error for $\sqrt{-1}$ and other negative square roots. A positive number squared is positive, a negative number squared is also positive, and $0^{2}=0$. No real number can therefore have a negative square.
